title: Sore throat, three days
notice: Synthetic conversation written for a software demo. Every name, date, phone number and address is invented. Not medical advice.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Good morning. I'm Doctor Kessler. Can I start by confirming your full name and date of birth?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Sure. It's Maria Alvarez, and my date of birth is March 4th, 1988.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Thanks, Maria. And is the best number to reach you still 416-555-0182?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Yes, that's my cell.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: And you're still at 42 Maple Crescent, Apartment 3, Toronto?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: That's right.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Great. So what brings you in today?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: My throat has been really sore for about three days now. It hurts a lot when I swallow, even water.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Have you had a fever?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I think so. Last night I took my temperature and it was 38.5. I've also had chills.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Any cough, runny nose, or stuffy nose?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: No, not really. No cough at all. It's mostly just my throat, and my neck feels kind of swollen.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Has anyone around you been sick?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: My roommate, Jenna, was diagnosed with strep throat last week.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Okay, that's helpful. Have you taken anything for it?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Just ibuprofen, 400 milligrams, maybe twice a day. It helps a little.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Any allergies to medications?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Yes, penicillin. I got hives from amoxicillin when I was a kid.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Good to know. Any other medical problems, or medications you take regularly?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: No, I'm usually healthy. I don't take anything regularly.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Alright, let me take a look. Your temperature here is 38.3, heart rate is 96, and blood pressure is 118 over 76. Open wide for me. Your tonsils are swollen and there's white exudate on both sides. The lymph nodes at the front of your neck are enlarged and tender. Your ears look normal, and your lungs are clear.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Is that bad?

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: It fits with strep throat. With the fever, the white patches, the swollen nodes and no cough, the chance is high, so I did a rapid strep swab while we were talking. It came back positive.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Okay, so it is strep, like Jenna.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Yes, this is strep pharyngitis. Normally I'd give amoxicillin, but because you had hives with it, I'm going to prescribe azithromycin instead, 500 milligrams once a day for five days.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Okay. Will that clear it up quickly?

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Most people feel better within two or three days. Please finish the whole course even if you feel better. You can keep taking ibuprofen for pain and fever, drink plenty of fluids, and warm salt water gargles can help.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Should I stay home from work?

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Yes. Stay home until you've been on the antibiotic for at least 24 hours and your fever is gone. I can give you a note for work.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: That would be great, thank you.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Come back, or go to the emergency department, if you have trouble breathing, can't swallow your own saliva, or can't open your mouth fully. And if you're not improving in 48 to 72 hours, give us a call.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Okay, I will.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: We'll send the prescription to your pharmacy. Feel better, Maria.
